rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`, and each has a real assertion.

- **Root resolution and owned result.**
  - `outline_content.rs#fn[selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits]` checks `file.select(&id.selector)`. It asserts the selected `id()` equals the requested id and `text()` is "second".
  - The same test checks `selected.select("")` returns the root with the original `id` and the full text.
  - `fn[rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes]` selects every outline item's selector. For each, it asserts `text()` equals the item's span slice and `structural_hash()` equals the item's hash.
  - `fn[unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items]` does the same for line items. It checks byte spans and text.
- **Shared snapshot and outline.**
  - `std::ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())` is asserted in the Rust test.
  - It is asserted in the Markdown test `fn[markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items]` too.
- **Fingerprinting rules.**
  - `fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` checks that selected content keeps the language, scheme and structural hash.
  - It also checks that a loaded and a supplied source give equal fingerprints.
  - A selection from a source built with a different scheme (`custom-v3`) gets a different fingerprint.
- **No re-read, usable after the original is dropped.**
  - The file handle is dropped and the file is rewritten.
  - The earlier selection still reports the original text and fingerprint.
  - A new `select("")` on that selection still returns the original contents, so no file read happened. `from_id` fails after the edit, which shows the file really changed.
- **Selector syntax, including the cited rules.**
  - Percent-encoded names are selected in the Markdown test. It uses `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and whitespace.
  - `#N` duplicates are selected, for Markdown sections and for CSS rules.
  - Anonymous `kind@hash` selectors are selected, for the Markdown block and the first section.
  - The plain-text test `fn[unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors]` selects an identical-line selector and gets "alpha".
  - `fn[ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines]` selects the identical "same" lines and succeeds.
- **Invalid, missing and ambiguous selections return errors.**
  - `fn[missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors]` asserts errors for the malformed selector `fn[` and the missing selector `fn[absent]`.
  - `fn[ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines]` asserts an "ambiguous" error for duplicate `part` items and for duplicate `line` items whose hashes differ.
  - `fn[css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent]` asserts an error for the un-numbered `rule[a%20b]`.
- **`text()` is the original text, before redaction.** `fn[formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans]` checks that a selected item's `text()` contains the raw token. It checks that `format()` is redacted.

The error content itself belongs to `requirements.sdk.outlines.errors` and the selector grammar to `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`. Both are cited as context. Their own tests assess them, and the selection tests apply them here. I found no gap and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineData;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
